examples.japanese: {大|おお}きな{手振|てぶ}りで{話|はな}す。
examples.english: To speak with large hand gestures.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{手振|てぶ}りを{交|まじ}えて{説明|せつめい}した。
examples.english: He explained while using hand gestures.

examples.japanese: {言葉|ことば}が{通|つう}じないので、{手振|てぶ}りと{身振|みぶ}りでコミュニケーションを{取|と}った。
examples.english: Since words didn't get through, we communicated using hand and body gestures.

notes:
Refers specifically to gestures made with the hands, often to emphasize speech or communicate without words. Frequently paired with {身振|みぶ}り (body gesture) in the set phrase {手振|てぶ}り{身振|みぶ}り.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {手振|てぶ}り{身振|みぶ}り: gestures and body language
- {手振|てぶ}りを{交|まじ}える: to mix in hand gestures
- {大|おお}きな{手振|てぶ}り: large/exaggerated gestures
- {手振|てぶ}りで{示|しめ}す: to indicate with a hand gesture

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {身振|みぶ}り: body gesture (broader — includes movement of the whole body)
- ジェスチャー: gesture (loanword, used broadly in casual speech)
- {合図|あいず}: signal (a deliberate, agreed-upon sign rather than spontaneous movement)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese communication tends to use fewer hand gestures than many Western cultures. However, certain gestures are distinctly Japanese, such as waving the hand in front of the face to indicate "no" or pointing to one's own nose to mean "me."
